newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Radio NZ strike to disrupt budget coverage.
newsitem.headline: Radio NZ strike to disrupt budget coverage.

text.p: Radio New Zealand's staff will commence strike action at midday on Thursday, disrupting its coverage of the budget delivery, NZPA reports.
Public Service Association (PSA) broadcast media members of Radio New Zealand will strike for 24 hours, after rejecting a three percent wage offer for two years.
Radio New Zealand chief executive Sharon Crosbie said on Wednesday radio broadcasters were fed up with changes in national radio, with the government, and a lack of money.
"The only thing we asked for was a two-year contract because we are between a rock and a hard place," she said.

Times would be difficult for a while because of a major transition period which included staff reviews and relocating to a new building. It was felt that a clear, two-year run would be needed for the changes, Crosbie said.
PSA organiser Malcolm Blair said a three percent rise for two years would amount to a pay cut as it would not keep pace with inflation.
